title: feat(dm): surface swallowed DAO bookkeeping failures via reporter port
body:
## Description

`DmRepository.recoverSelfWrap` and `_finalizeAfterRecipient{Success,Failure}` swallow DAO write failures via `Log.error` only. Today there's no production signal for how often these doubly-degraded paths fire — Crashlytics never sees them, because (a) the catches live in repository code (not a Bloc), and (b) the `dm_repository` package can't depend on `openvine/observability` without inverting the layer boundary.

This PR introduces an **error-reporter port** on `DmRepository` that the app wires through to `CrashReportingService.recordError`, and applies the matching service-layer and bloc-layer signals so the full DM retry chain becomes observable.

**How it works**

1. `DmRepository` gains a `DmRepositoryErrorReporter?` typedef constructor parameter — a `void Function(Object, StackTrace, {required String site})`. Each of the 7 swallow sites invokes the reporter after the existing `Log.error`. Sites are addressed via the new `DmRepositoryReportableSites` constants so Crashlytics aggregates by `reason: 'DmRepository.<site>'`.
2. `dmRepositoryProvider` (in `app_providers.dart`) wires the closure to forward to `CrashReportingService.instance.recordError(...)`. The singleton is captured by reference — stable across `ref.watch` rebuilds, no `ValueKey`-on-identity treatment needed.
3. `OutgoingDmRetryService` gains an optional `CrashReportingService?` constructor parameter (singleton-default, mirroring `DivineBlocObserver`) and reports its two existing `Log.error`-only catches — per-row throw and top-level sweep failure.
4. `ConversationBloc._onSelfWrapRecoveryRequested`'s raw `addError(lastError, …)` is upgraded to `addError(Reportable(lastError, context: '_onSelfWrapRecoveryRequested'), …)` so the bloc-level failure also flows to Crashlytics through `DivineBlocObserver`.

The previously-silent inner swallow inside `recoverSelfWrap`'s JSON-parse error handler also gains a matching `Log.error` so the unified log stays consistent across all 7 sites.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4127

## Out of Scope

- Durable counter on `outgoing_dms` (rejected — schema migration risk; in-app counter defeats the "invisible without proactive checking" purpose of the issue).
- Sibling swallows in `nip17_message_service.dart` (different scope; tracked separately).
- Extracting a shared `openvine_observability` package (correct long-term move, but YAGNI for one repo today).
- `recoverFullSend` observability — will reuse the same port when #4240 lands.
- Lifting `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` out of the outer transaction — changes atomicity semantics; the outer-catch site at line 962 is sufficient for the rate signal.

## Verification

From `mobile/`:

- ` ✅ dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed` on all 10 touched files (no diffs)
- ` ✅ flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — No issues found
- ` ✅ flutter analyze` in `packages/dm_repository` — No issues found

- ` ✅ flutter test test/providers/` — 554 tests pass (sanity on provider wiring)
- ` ✅ dm_repository line coverage: 94.21%` (above the 93% CI gate)

title: DM: surface swallowed DAO bookkeeping failures in self-wrap recovery paths
body:
## Summary

`DmRepository.recoverSelfWrap` and `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` swallow DAO bookkeeping failures via `Log.error` only. Crashlytics doesn't see them because the wrapped errors are not `Reportable` per `.claude/rules/error_handling.md`. Today we have no signal for how often these doubly-degraded paths fire in production.

## Problem

The doubly-degraded path in `recoverSelfWrap` (publish landed; both `deleteById` and fallback `markSelfWrapStatus(sent)` threw) is documented as safe via NIP-17 receive-side dedup — but "safe" is hypothesis until we measure. Same for any DAO write failure inside the recipient-success finalize path. We currently have no way to know if this is happening 0/day or 100/day.

## Desired Outcome

Surface DAO bookkeeping failures in these recovery paths so they're visible in monitoring without flooding Crashlytics.

## Scope

Decide between:

1. **Wrap as `Reportable`** per the matrix in `.claude/rules/error_handling.md`. These are arguably "programming-invariant violations" once the publish has landed — the row should always be writeable. Risk: Crashlytics noise on transient SQLite contention.
2. **Counter / debug surface only.** Increment a metric, expose under a debug screen. Less noisy, but invisible without proactive checking.
3. **Both.** Counter for triage, `Reportable` only on persistent runs (e.g., N consecutive failures for the same rumor).

## Context

- Two specific call sites today, both in `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart`: `recoverSelfWrap` doubly-degraded catch, plus any throw inside `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` (currently upstream of any try/catch on the caller side).
- Spotted during PR #4106 review by Liz; follow-up to #4102.

title: Fix user reports emitting invalid NIP-56 e tags
body:
## Problem

Mobile user-report events can emit invalid NIP-56 report targets.

`ContentReportingService.reportUser()` falls back to a synthetic event id when no related event is provided:

```dart
final eventId = (relatedEventIds != null && relatedEventIds.isNotEmpty)
    ? relatedEventIds.first
    : 'user_$userPubkey';
```

That value is then used as the NIP-56 `e` tag in `_createReportingEvent()`:

```dart
['e', eventId, nip56Type],
['p', authorPubkey, nip56Type],
```

For DM user reports, `ConversationActionsCubit.reportUser()` calls `reportUser()` without `relatedEventIds`, producing kind `1984` events like:

```text
e tag: user_<64-char-pubkey>
p tag: <64-char-pubkey>
```

This is not a valid event id. Funnelcake currently aggregates report events through `report_counts_mv`, which expects `e` tag targets to be 64-char event ids. In production, ClickHouse has stored kind `1984` report events with invalid `e` targets matching this mobile format, for example:

```text
user_e680e1c186eb8d618dbd5db1e18ec4b84fdd79fddb3987692f640a33a09cf3db
```

Those malformed report events can cause Funnelcake insert failures when `report_counts_mv` tries to write the target into `FixedString(64)`.

## Scope

Update mobile user-report event construction so user reports do not place `user_<pubkey>` in a NIP-56 `e` tag.

Suggested behavior:

- For user reports with no related event id, use the `p` tag as the target and omit the `e` tag.
- For user reports with one or more real related event ids, include valid `e` tags only for actual 64-char event ids.
- Preserve the `p` tag with the reported user's pubkey and the NIP-56 report type.
- Preserve existing local report history and user-facing report flow behavior.

## Relevant Code

- `mobile/lib/services/content_reporting_service.dart`
- `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/conversation_actions/conversation_actions_cubit.dart`
- Related dialog path: `mobile/lib/widgets/report_content_dialog.dart`

## Test Plan

- Add or update unit tests for `ContentReportingService.reportUser()` with no `relatedEventIds`.
- Assert the produced kind `1984` event does not contain an `e` tag with `user_<pubkey>`.
- Assert the produced event includes a `p` tag for the reported user pubkey with the report type.
- Add/update tests for `reportUser()` with valid related event ids and assert only valid event ids are emitted as `e` tags.
- Add/update tests for DM conversation user reporting to cover the no-related-event path.
- Manually verify reporting a DM user still succeeds from the UI.

## Dependency / Coordination Notes

Funnelcake should also defensively filter `report_counts_mv` to ignore malformed `e` targets, because relays should not rely on all clients being well-formed. This mobile issue fixes the known client-side producer of `user_<pubkey>` `e` tags.

title: feat(dm): recoverFullSend primitive + auto-sweep wiring for recipient-failed DMs
body:
## Description

Closes #4240. Final follow-up in the #3909 stack for the durable
outgoing-DM queue. With this change, `outgoing_dms` rows that finalize
as `recipient_wrap_status: failed` are auto-recovered by the
`OutgoingDmRetryService` foreground sweep instead of sitting idle on
the queue.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4240. Relates to #3909, epic #3912.

### What the gap looked like

`OutgoingDmRetryService` (PR #4241) shipped with a counting-only branch
for `recipient: failed` rows — the inline comment said `recovery
primitive lands in #4240`. Without that primitive, an app kill or
relay reject that finalized as recipient-failed left the row queued
indefinitely (only manual SnackBar retry, which mints a new rumor and
zombifies the original row, could recover).

### What this PR ships

Two commits, layered bottom-up:

**1. `feat(dm): add recoverFullSend primitive` — repository layer**

`DmRepository.recoverFullSend(rumorId)` mirrors `recoverSelfWrap`'s
shape:

- Validates ownership against `_userPubkey` (multi-account isolation).
- Idempotent: if `recipientWrapStatus == sent` already (concurrent
  recovery raced ahead, or the original partial-success path promoted
  the row), defers to `recoverSelfWrap` so the recipient wrap is
  never republished.
- Rebuilds the rumor from `rumor_event_json` (preserves receiver-side
  dedup key across retries — minting a fresh rumor would defeat it).
- Calls `_messageService.sendRumor`, then finalizes via the existing
  `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` / `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure`
  helpers.
- On full success: inserts `direct_messages` + upserts the
  conversation row + deletes the queue row inside one
  `runInTransaction` — same atomicity contract as `sendMessage`'s
  happy path.
- On partial success: keeps the row at `recipient: sent / self:
  failed` so the next sweep replays the missing self-wrap via
  `recoverSelfWrap`.
- On recipient failure: re-marks both wraps failed with the new error.

Re-publishing a rumor whose original wire copy actually landed is
safe at the protocol level: NIP-17 receiver-side dedup keys on the
rumor id, preserved verbatim through `rumor_event_json`.

**2. `feat(dm): wire recoverFullSend into OutgoingDmRetryService` — service layer**

Strategy table after this change:

| Row state                          | Recovery primitive    |
|------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| `recipient: sent / self: failed`   | `recoverSelfWrap`     |
| `recipient: failed`                | `recoverFullSend`     |
| `pending: pending`                 | not in retryable filter; deferred |

The dispatch reuses the existing per-row backoff, `_isSweeping`
re-entrancy guard, and the `StateError` / `ArgumentError` /
unexpected-throw error policy from the `recoverSelfWrap` branch.

Sweep summary log gains `full-send-recovered=N full-send-failed=N`,
replacing the now-acted-on `recipient-failed=N` line. The class doc
comment is updated to state both strategy entries.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

These came up during the design but are explicitly deferred:

- **Pending-row recovery.** `pending: pending` rows (true app-kill
  mid-publish, no finalize wrote) remain out of
  `getRetryableForOwner`'s filter and are not handled here. The DAO's
  `getStillPendingForOwner` is the read primitive for that path; the
  open design questions (queuedAt time-gate to avoid stealing
  in-flight sends, cold-start-only trigger, whether to reuse
  `recoverFullSend` or split) belong in their own issue. Will file
  under epic #3912.
- **Observability for `recoverFullSend`'s swallowed paths.** PR #4402
  is wiring the `DmRepositoryErrorReporter` port across the existing
  7 swallow sites; once that merges, adding the 1-2 new sites in
  `recoverFullSend` is a one-line follow-up. Out of this PR to avoid
  a coordination dependency.
- **Manual-retry zombie cleanup.** Today, tapping Retry on the
  `failed` SnackBar (#3908) dispatches `ConversationMessageSent`,
  which mints a fresh rumor and a fresh queue row, zombifying the
  original failed row until auto-sweep exhausts its retries. Routing
  that path through `recoverFullSend(rumorId)` on the existing row is
  the right cleanup but expands UX surface beyond #4240's scope —
  separate PR.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Verification

From `mobile/`:

- [x] `dart format` — no diffs.
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean.
- [x] `flutter analyze packages/dm_repository` — clean.
- [x] `flutter test packages/dm_repository` — **232 / 232 passing**
  (10 new `recoverFullSend` tests).
- [x] `flutter test test/services/outgoing_dm_retry_service_test.dart`
  — **27 / 27 passing** (6 new tests + 1 reworked).
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/dm test/screens/inbox
  test/services/outgoing_dm_retry_service_test.dart` — **359 / 359
  passing** (no regressions in adjacent DM bloc / view tests).

### Pinning contracts added

- `recoverFullSend` never invokes `sendRumor` when `recipientWrapStatus
  == sent` (idempotent guard defers to `recoverSelfWrap`).
- `recoverFullSend` never inserts into `direct_messages` on recipient
  publish failure.
- Sweep dispatches `recoverFullSend` for `recipient: failed` rows.
- Sweep dispatches `recoverSelfWrap` for `recipient: sent / self:
  failed` rows.
- Sweep never invokes `sendMessage` / `sendGroupMessage` for any
  retryable row (would zombify the queue row by enqueueing a new id).
- `recoverFullSend` is never invoked for rows where `recipient: sent`
  (those route through `recoverSelfWrap`).

### Manual verification (please confirm during review)

- [ ] Force a recipient publish failure on a 1:1 send (e.g. block the
      first `publishEvent` round in a debug build). Row finalizes at
      `recipient: failed / self: failed`. Background then re-foreground
      the app → row is recovered automatically → `direct_messages` row
      appears → queue row deleted.
- [ ] Same scenario but with sustained relay reject → row exhausts
      retries (5 attempts with 2s → 5min backoff) → falls out of
      `getRetryableForOwner`.
- [ ] Cross-account safety: send from account A, switch to account B,
      foreground → A's failed row is **not** recovered while B is
      active.
- [ ] Partial-delivery recovery still works (#4106 + #4241
      regression): force a self-wrap-only failure → SnackBar offers
      Retry → next foreground also sweeps it via `recoverSelfWrap` if
      the user dismisses the SnackBar.

## Acceptance check for closing #3909

After this PR lands:

| AC                                                       | Status |
|----------------------------------------------------------|--------|
| 1. Survives app kill mid-send + auto-recovers           | ✅ for `recipient: failed`. Pending-row case deferred to follow-up. |
| 2. Partial-delivery visibly distinguished + recoverable | ✅ (#4106) |
| 3. #3908 tests stay green                                | ✅ |
| 4. New tests cover the matrix (DAO / repo / service)    | ✅ |
| 5. No regression in the SnackBar retry flow             | ✅ |

title: DM: add recoverFullSend primitive for recipient-wrap-failed outgoing_dms rows
body:
## Summary

`outgoing_dms` rows can land in `recipient_wrap_status: failed / self_wrap_status: failed` state when the recipient gift-wrap publish itself fails (set by `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure` in `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart`). Today there is no recovery primitive for this state — only `recoverSelfWrap` exists (PR #4106), and it is for the `recipient: sent / self: failed` case only.

## Problem

The new `OutgoingDmRetryService` from #4124 enumerates these recipient-failed rows and logs a count, but does not act on them. They sit on the queue until the user manually re-sends, or until `retry_count` reaches `maxRetries` and they fall out of the retryable filter. The `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure` comment ("both wrap statuses remain retryable on the queue row") promises auto-retry that does not yet exist.

## Desired Outcome

Add a `DmRepository.recoverFullSend(rumorId)` primitive that re-runs the full `sendRumor` (recipient + self) for a stored row, persisting `direct_messages` on success and updating queue-row status by outcome — the same shape as `sendMessage`'s success and partial paths.

Wire the primitive into the `OutgoingDmRetryService` strategy table as the second entry: `recipient: failed` rows dispatch to `recoverFullSend`.

## Scope

- New `NIP17MessageService.publishFullSend` (or reuse `sendRumor` directly) for an already-built rumor — same integration shape as `publishSelfWrap` from PR #4106.
- New `DmRepository.recoverFullSend(rumorId)` that:
  - Looks up the row by id, validates ownership (mirror `recoverSelfWrap`'s account-scope check).
  - Rebuilds the rumor from `rumor_event_json`.
  - Calls `sendRumor` (or `publishFullSend`).
  - On success: runs the same `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` + atomic `direct_messages` insert that `sendMessage` does on its happy path.
  - On failure: marks both wraps `failed` and bumps retry — same shape as `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure`.
  - Idempotent: short-circuits if `recipientWrapStatus == sent` (a prior recovery already landed and the row has since been demoted to a self-wrap-only retry case — call `recoverSelfWrap` instead).
- Strategy-table wiring in `OutgoingDmRetryService` so `recipient: failed` rows are recovered the same way `recipient: sent / self: failed` rows are today.
- Tests pin: no double-publish to recipient if the prior attempt's recipient publish actually landed but local persistence failed; no duplicate `direct_messages` row inserted; sweep dispatches the right primitive per row state.

## Edge cases to design carefully

- **Recipient publish actually landed but local persistence failed last time.** The previous `_finalizeAfterRecipientFailure` marks both wraps failed pessimistically — in this case, `recoverFullSend` would re-publish to the recipient. The receiver-side NIP-17 dedup keys on rumor id (preserved across retries via `rumor_event_json`) bound this to a duplicate gift wrap rather than a duplicate visible message, but it is still wasted bandwidth. Decide whether the design should query the relay for the rumor-id-tagged gift wrap before re-publishing.
- **App killed mid-publish (`pending: pending` rows).** Out of scope for #4124's `getRetryableForOwner` filter; covered by `getStillPendingForOwner` instead. Decide whether `recoverFullSend` covers both cases (state B and state C from the brainstorm) or whether state C gets its own primitive.

## Context

- Brainstorm that surfaced this gap: `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-10-issue4124-outgoing-dm-auto-sweep-brainstorm.md`.
- Production telemetry will come from #4124's enumeration log (`Log.info('OutgoingDmRetryService sweep complete: ... recipient-failed=N')`). Use those counts to prioritize this work.
- Sister issue #4127 covers Crashlytics surfacing for the doubly-degraded paths inside `recoverSelfWrap` and `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` — coordinate so this work does not duplicate that error-reporting decision.
- Parent epic: #3912 (DM reliability hardening).

title: search: define canonical focus behavior across Explore and Search Results
body:
## Summary

Search needs a defined and testable focus model across Explore and Search Results. Today, routing during partial input can cause keyboard/focus continuity to break.

Parent epic: #3801

## Agent Brief

This issue is about **focus and keyboard continuity**, not search quality.

Confirmed:
- Explore auto-navigates while the user is still typing.
- The destination search screen is created with a non-empty `initialQuery`.
- The destination field only auto-focuses when `initialQuery` is empty.
- Users have to manually bring the keyboard back.

## Confirmed facts

From code:
- `ExploreScreen._onSearchChanged()` pushes the search route on partial input.
- `SearchResultsAppBar` requests focus only when `initialQuery` is empty.

From issue history:
- #3020 already tracks the user-visible keyboard collapse symptom.

## Problem

We do not have a canonical search focus model. The current behavior is partly implicit and route-driven, which makes it hard to reason about and easy to regress.

## Questions to resolve

- If we navigate during typing, should focus transfer to the destination field automatically?
- If we require explicit submit to navigate, what should happen to focus before and after submit?
- Should keyboard continuity be guaranteed across all search entry points or only Explore?

## Acceptance criteria

- Search focus behavior is explicitly defined for Explore and Search Results.
- Keyboard continuity behavior is intentional and documented.
- The chosen behavior is covered by automated tests.
- #3020 can be resolved against this contract rather than ad hoc UI behavior.

title: fix(push): send push control events to Divine relay with relay OK handling
body:
## Summary

Push registration could look successful even when the Divine relay never accepted the event.
This change sends push registration, deregistration, and preference events directly to the configured Divine relay and waits for a relay OK response.
It also keeps the publish bounded so a late relay connection cannot write or queue a stale push-control event after the timeout.

## What Changed

Push control events now use the same targeted OK-confirmed publish path.
The relay layer now treats the caller timeout as one deadline for both sending and waiting for OK responses.
Same-URL fallback now distinguishes a failed send from a sent frame, and deadline-bound sends cannot queue stale EVENT messages.

- Route kinds 3079, 3080, and 3083 through `publishEventAwaitOk` with `targetRelays: [EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl]`.
- Let explicit target-relay OK publishes run even when the general relay pool has no connected relays.
- Skip the generic disconnected-relay retry when explicit target relays are provided.
- Bound `RelayPool.sendEventAwaitOk` with one deadline across `_sendCollect` plus OK waiting.
- Thread that deadline through `Relay.send`, `RelayBase.send`, and `WebSocketConnectionManager.sendJson`.
- Disable pending-message queueing for deadline-bound await-OK sends.
- Do not queue pending-auth messages for deadline-bound await-OK sends.
- Remove expired temp relays after deadline timeout so their connection waiters cannot flush stale control events.
- Track expected relays as soon as each send succeeds, so timeouts report the relays that actually received the frame.
- Avoid retrying a stalled same-URL normal target as a temp relay after the shared deadline is consumed.
- Allow same-URL temp fallback when the normal target path returns `false` immediately without sending.
- Log accepted, rejected, and no-response relay outcomes without logging encrypted push-control content.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4411

## Testing

I tested the push-control service paths, the client OK-publish wrapper, and the relay-pool timeout and fallback behavior.
I also verified the touched packages and the app analyzer after the SDK API change.

- `dart format packages/nostr_client/lib/src/nostr_client.dart packages/nostr_client/test/src/nostr_client_test.dart packages/nostr_sdk/lib/relay/relay_pool.dart packages/nostr_sdk/test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart`
- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib/relay/relay.dart lib/relay/relay_base.dart lib/relay/relay_isolate.dart lib/relay/web_socket_connection_manager.dart lib/relay/relay_pool.dart test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart test/unit/relay_pool_auth_test.dart test/unit/relay_count_test.dart test/integration/relay_auth_test.dart test/integration/nip50_search_test.dart`
- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed test/src/follow_repository_test.dart`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/src/nostr_client_test.dart --plain-name "publishEventAwaitOk"`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart --plain-name "sendEventAwaitOk"`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart`
- `dart test test/unit/publish_outcome_test.dart`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/services/push_notification_service_test.dart`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/providers/push_notification_sync_test.dart`
- `dart analyze` in `mobile/packages/nostr_sdk`
- `flutter analyze --no-pub` in `mobile/packages/nostr_client`
- `flutter analyze --no-pub` in `mobile/packages/follow_repository`
- `flutter analyze --no-pub` in `mobile`
- `flutter test --no-pub` in `mobile`
- `git diff --check`

## Risks

The main behavior change is that explicit target publishes no longer wait for unrelated pool reconnects, and deadline-bound OK publishes no longer queue messages for later delivery.
That is intentional for push control events because a late queued control event can make the app report a failed publish while still mutating relay-side push state later.
The SDK `Relay.send` interface now accepts an optional deadline, so custom test relays and package-local fake relays were updated to match.

- A target URL already present in the normal relay pool is not retried as a temp relay after the normal path sends or queues the frame.
- A normal target path that returns `false` immediately can still fall back to a same-URL temp relay within the caller timeout.
- If the normal target path stalls until the shared deadline is exhausted, the publish fails fast instead of trying the same URL a second way.
- If a relay connects after the deadline, the deadline-aware send path returns false before writing the stale EVENT.
- This does not prove the push service processed the event after relay acceptance; it only confirms relay acceptance.

title: perf(inbox): remove N+1 latest-message overlay queries in DmRepository
body:
## Summary

Closes #4296 

PR #4286 introduced a correctness fix for stale inbox previews but created an N+1 read-path problem: every `watchAcceptedConversations` / `watchPotentialRequests` emission performed one `getMessagesForConversation(limit: 1)` query per conversation. This PR removes that fan-out while keeping the correctness guarantee.

## Changes

### Option A — batched overlay query (`db_client`)
`getLatestMessagesForConversations` was already added in the review feedback of #4286. `_overlayLatestMessages` now issues a **single** batched query per emit regardless of conversation count, down from N.

### Option B — write-path drift fix (`ConversationsDao`)
Root cause of the original staleness: `upsertConversation` used `insertOnConflictUpdate` which unconditionally overwrote `last_message_*` columns on every gift-wrap arrival, including older out-of-order ones during backfill.

`upsertConversation` now uses a conditional `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` that only updates the three last-message columns when the incoming `last_message_timestamp` is **strictly newer** than the stored value. A `forceUpdateLastMessage` parameter bypasses the guard for `_refreshConversationPreview` (post-deletion), where the replacement message is by definition the newest remaining one.

`current_user_has_sent` is also now a write-once ratchet at the SQL level (`false → true` only, never reversed).

The `DoUpdate.withExcluded` rewrite also makes the rest of the conflict contract explicit and typed: `subject`, `ownerPubkey`, and `dmProtocol` preserve the existing non-null value when an incoming upsert omits them, while incoming non-null values still overwrite; `createdAt` remains immutable after the row is first created.

### Transitional overlay
`_overlayLatestMessages` is kept as a read-path safety net for existing user databases that may have stale rows written before the write-path fix shipped. Removal is tracked in #4407 (requires a backfill migration).

## Tests

- **7 `ConversationsDao` tests**: out-of-order upsert does not overwrite a newer preview; in-order upsert does update; `forceUpdateLastMessage: true` bypasses the guard; `currentUserHasSent` is never flipped back to false; nullable conflict fields preserve existing values when omitted; nullable conflict fields overwrite when provided; `createdAt` stays immutable on conflict.
- **Existing overlay regression tests** from #4286 remain intact: overlay preview, re-sort by timestamp, file-message preview.
- Updated `dm_repository_test` stubs/verify calls to include the new `forceUpdateLastMessage` parameter.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Inbox streams no longer perform one `getMessagesForConversation(limit: 1)` per conversation per emit
- [x] Inbox preview still shows true latest message even when the conversation row is stale
- [x] Ordering remains based on the real latest message timestamp
- [x] Existing regression coverage intact
- [x] Transitional code has a linked `TODO(perf4407)` pointing at #4407 with a clear removal plan

Mobile push control events need to reliably reach the Divine relay path consumed by `divine-push-service` so real FCM push registration, deregistration, and preference updates work in production.

## Context
Recent investigation found:

- PR #4162 fixes the signer-readiness race by delaying registration until a signer-backed Nostr session is ready.
- A prod-emulator test showed generic relay-pool publishing could report success while the kind `3079` event landed on a user relay (`nos.lol`) instead of `relay.divine.video`.
- A targeted diagnostic run against `wss://relay.divine.video` showed the relay rejected `3079` with `blocked: kind 3079 not in allowed list`.
- Relay-side allowlist/discovery work is tracked in `divine-funnelcake#380`.
- First-party mobile does not publish kind `1` events today.
- Mobile consumes kind `1` for mention-style notifications.
- Mobile comments/replies are currently published as kind `1111`.
- This issue should not expand mobile push preferences to `1111` or `30023`.

## Scope
- Publish push control events directly to `EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl`.
- Await NIP-20 relay `OK` for push control events.
- Use a bounded `5s` relay OK timeout.
- Log relay outcomes:
  - `acceptedBy`
  - `rejectedBy`
  - `noResponseFrom`
- Apply targeted relay + OK behavior to:
  - `3079` push registration.
  - `3080` push deregistration.
  - `3083` push preferences.
- Preserve the readiness-driven registration lifecycle from PR #4162.
- Preserve token-refresh re-registration behavior, but make refreshed-token registration use the same targeted relay + OK path.
- Keep `p` tags targeting `EnvironmentConfig.pushServicePubkey`.
- Keep existing `NotificationPreferences` trigger kind list unchanged for now: `[1, 3, 7, 16]`.
- Add temporary relay-layer diagnostics for push control kinds `3079/3080/3083` during rollout.
- Keep permanent push-control logs in `PushNotificationService`.
- Do not add a durable retry/background scheduler in this issue.

## Current Mobile Kind Contract Notes
- `1`: consumed for mention-style notifications; not first-party published by mobile; not current comments/replies.
- `3`: follows/contact-list.
- `7`: likes/reactions.
- `16`: generic reposts.
- `1111`: current mobile comments/replies, but not yet advertised in `3083` preferences.
- `30023`: mobile can consume long-form mentions locally, but not yet advertised in `3083` preferences.

## Out of Scope
- Adding `1111` to mobile push preferences.
- Adding `30023` to mobile push preferences.
- Changing canonical notification trigger-kind policy.
- Adding relay-side allowlist changes.
- Adding durable retry queues or background retry scheduling.
- Hardening relay policy to require `p` tags for push control kinds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `3079` registration targets `EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl` and awaits/logs relay OK/reject/no-response.
- [ ] Token-refresh registration uses the same targeted relay + OK handling.
- [ ] `3080` deregistration targets `EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl` and awaits/logs relay OK/reject/no-response.
- [ ] `3083` preferences targets `EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl` and awaits/logs relay OK/reject/no-response.
- [ ] Push control publishes use a bounded `5s` relay OK timeout.
- [ ] Current `NotificationPreferences.toKindsList()` remains `[1, 3, 7, 16]` by default.
- [ ] No new durable retry/background scheduler is introduced.
- [ ] Temporary relay-layer diagnostics are limited to push control kinds `3079/3080/3083`.

## Test Plan
- Unit test `3079` registration targets `EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl`.
- Unit test `3079` registration awaits relay OK and handles accepted outcome.
- Unit test `3079` registration handles relay rejection without throwing and logs rejection reason.
- Unit test `3079` registration handles relay no-response timeout without throwing and logs `noResponseFrom`.
- Unit test token-refresh registration uses targeted relay + OK handling.
- Unit test `3080` deregistration targets `EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl`.
- Unit test `3080` deregistration awaits relay OK and handles accepted/rejected/no-response outcomes.
- Unit test `3083` preferences target `EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl`.
- Unit test `3083` preferences await relay OK and handle accepted/rejected/no-response outcomes.
- Unit test current `NotificationPreferences.toKindsList()` remains `[1, 3, 7, 16]` by default.
- Manual prod-emulator verification after `divine-funnelcake#380` is deployed:
  - Sign in with an allowlisted key.
  - Confirm `3079` receives `OK true` from `wss://relay.divine.video`.
  - Confirm `divine-push-service` observes registration.
  - Confirm backend stores token metadata.
  - Confirm registration does not rely on user relays such as `nos.lol`.
  - Confirm logs show target relay, relay OK result, and push-service processing evidence.

## Dependencies
- Depends on `divine-funnelcake#380` or equivalent deployment allowing push control kinds on `relay.divine.video`:
  - `3079`
  - `3080`
  - `3083`
- `divine-funnelcake#380` should also advertise newly allowed control kinds in discovery metadata.
- `divine-push-service` should continue to validate/decrypt/process:
  - `3079` registration.
  - `3080` deregistration.
  - `3083` preferences.
- Relay `OK true` only proves relay acceptance/storage/broadcast. It does not prove `divine-push-service` decrypted or persisted the registration, so manual verification must check both relay OK and push-service registration storage/logs.
- Future `divine-push-service` contract cleanup should decide:
  - Whether kind `1` should remain a push trigger for text-note mentions.
  - Whether comments/replies should use kind `1111` as a push trigger.
  - Whether long-form mentions should use `30023`.
  - Whether/when mobile should advertise `1111` and/or `30023` in `3083` preferences.

title: perf(inbox): remove N+1 latest-message overlay queries in DmRepository
body:
## Summary
PR #4286 adds a read-time workaround in `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart` to repair stale inbox preview data by overlaying each conversation row with the actual latest message from `direct_messages`.

That workaround fixes correctness, but it introduces a new performance problem: every emission from `watchAcceptedConversations()` and `watchPotentialRequests()` now performs one `DirectMessagesDao.getMessagesForConversation(..., limit: 1)` query per conversation.

For users with many conversations, this turns a single conversations-stream update into an N+1 fan-out of DAO reads.

## Current implementation
PR #4286 changes these paths:
- `watchAcceptedConversations()` -> `.asyncMap(_overlayLatestMessages)`
- `watchPotentialRequests()` -> `.asyncMap(_overlayLatestMessages)`

`_overlayLatestMessages()` then does:
- iterate every `ConversationRow`
- call `getMessagesForConversation(row.id, limit: 1, ownerPubkey: _ownerPubkey)`
- copy the latest message fields back onto the domain model
- resort the list in memory by the overlaid timestamp

Relevant code in the PR:
- `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart:1667-1698`

## Why this matters
The workaround runs on every stream tick, not just on first load.

That means:
- 10 conversations -> 10 extra DAO reads per emit
- 100 conversations -> 100 extra DAO reads per emit
- every accepted-conversations refresh and every potential-requests refresh pays this cost

Even if the reads are parallelized with `Future.wait`, the app still performs one query per conversation, plus an in-memory resort, on every update. This is avoidable read amplification on a hot inbox path.

## Root cause
The comment added in PR #4286 documents the underlying correctness problem well: the denormalized `conversations.lastMessageContent` / `lastMessageTimestamp` fields can drift out of sync with the real latest message in `direct_messages`.

The overlay is compensating for write-path drift at read time.

## Desired outcome
Keep the correctness fix, but remove the per-conversation query fan-out.

## Candidate fixes
### Option A: batched latest-message query
Add a DAO method that fetches the latest message for many conversation ids in one query, for example:
- `getLatestMessagesForConversations(List<String> conversationIds, {required String ownerPubkey})`

Then replace the N queries in `_overlayLatestMessages()` with a single batched read and a map/join in memory.

### Option B: fix denormalized-column drift at the write path
Investigate why `conversations.lastMessageContent` and `lastMessageTimestamp` become stale during backfill / out-of-order gift-wrap arrival.

If the write path can guarantee the denormalized columns always reflect the actual latest message, the overlay can be removed entirely and the existing conversation-watch queries can remain the source of truth.

### Option C: hybrid transition
Ship a batched DAO read first to remove the N+1 cost, then follow with a write-path correctness fix and delete the overlay once the denormalized columns are trustworthy again.

## Acceptance criteria
- Inbox conversation streams no longer perform one `getMessagesForConversation(... limit: 1)` call per conversation on every emit.
- The inbox preview still shows the true latest message even when the conversation row is stale.
- Ordering remains based on the real latest message timestamp.
- Existing regression coverage for stale preview overlay remains intact or is updated to cover the new batched/corrected implementation.
- If the final fix relies on transitional code, include a linked `TODO(#issue)` with a clear removal plan.

## Regression tests to preserve
The tests added in PR #4286 should remain conceptually covered:
- overlays the latest message from `DirectMessageRow` over the denormalized row preview
- re-sorts conversations by the actual latest message timestamp
- file-message preview overlay behavior

## Context
Introduced while reviewing PR #4286.

This issue tracks removing the new N+1 inbox read-path debt without losing the correctness fix that motivated it.

title: fix(android): default useLegacySurface to true to close FlutterJNI renderer race (#3416)
body:
## Description

Closes #3416. Crashlytics issue `d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a` (regressed on 1.0.13 build 502 — Samsung SM-S918W).

```
java.lang.RuntimeException: Cannot execute operation because FlutterJNI is not attached to native.
  at io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterJNI.ensureAttachedToNative
  at io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterJNI.scheduleFrame
  at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer.scheduleEngineFrame
  at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer$ImageReaderSurfaceProducer.onImage
  at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer$ImageReaderSurfaceProducer$PerImageReader.lambda$new$0
  at android.media.ImageReader$1.run
```

### Root cause

PR #3762 narrowed the race between `ExoPlayer`'s decoder pipeline and `TextureRegistry.SurfaceProducer.ImageReader` callback dispatch — but explicitly acknowledged a residual 1–2 frame window (`stop()` and `clearVideoSurface()` are async; in-flight `MediaCodec` output can still land in a detaching `ImageReader`, and the `onImage` callback then invokes `FlutterJNI.scheduleFrame()` after `FlutterJNI` is detached). On Samsung SM-S918W's fast decoder, that residual fires.

Five callsites in the app use `useTexture: true` and **inherit the default** `useLegacySurface: false`, opting them — accidentally — into the SurfaceProducer/ImageReader path:

- `mobile/lib/widgets/video_editor/main_editor/video_editor_canvas.dart:443`
- `mobile/lib/screens/video_metadata/video_metadata_preview_screen.dart:82`
- `mobile/lib/screens/video_metadata/video_metadata_cover_screen.dart:72`
- `mobile/lib/widgets/video_clip/video_clip_preview.dart:61`
- `mobile/lib/widgets/video_metadata/modes/classic/video_metadata_classic_preview_thumbnail.dart:81`

`infinite_video_feed.dart:654–657` explicitly sets `useLegacySurface: true` and is the only callsite that's safe today. The original `SurfaceProducer` motivation (PR #3856) was the feed's Vivo/Android-16 compat, but PR #3242 migrated the feed to `infinite_video_feed` (legacy surface) — so nothing in the repo currently needs `SurfaceProducer` for its intended purpose; it's in use only via the unsafe default.

### Fix

Flip the Dart-side default of `useLegacySurface` from `false` to `true` (one-line behaviour change + docstring rewrite). All five accidentally-vulnerable callsites inherit the safe default and stop hitting the race in one change. SurfaceProducer remains available via explicit `useLegacySurface: false` for callsites that genuinely need OEM surface-recreate callbacks — there are none today.

| Site | Change |
|---|---|
| `divine_video_player_controller.dart:51` | `useLegacySurface = true` (was `false`) |
| `divine_video_player_controller.dart:27–46` | Docstring rewritten to document the new default and the explicit opt-in for SurfaceProducer trade-off |
| `DivineVideoPlayerInstance.kt:176–193` | KDoc on `enableTextureOutput` rewritten to flip the "(default)" annotation. Kotlin function default stays at `false` — Dart always passes the value over MethodChannel, so the native default is unreachable in production. |

The 5 vulnerable callsites are intentionally **not** edited — they now inherit the safe default automatically. This keeps the diff minimal and documents that the fix is at the API layer, not the callsite layer.

### Why this is a complete fix for #3416

- The crash signature is fundamentally a race between Flutter SDK's internal `ImageReaderSurfaceProducer.onImage` (inside `FlutterRenderer`, outside our code) and `FlutterJNI` detach.
- The race cannot be closed from inside the SurfaceProducer disposal path without invasive `MediaCodec.flush()` reflection (rejected as overkill by PR #3762).
- It **can** be closed by ensuring no app callsite uses the SurfaceProducer/ImageReader path. After this fix, no `lib/` callsite does — and the safe choice is now the default, so future code is protected too.
- PR #3762's three-layer disposal hardening (Instance.dispose, Plugin.onDetachedFromActivity, PlatformView.dispose) is preserved unchanged — it remains the contract for any explicit `useLegacySurface: false` opt-in.

## Reproduction (pre-fix)

1. Real Android device (the crash signature is most reliably reproduced on devices with fast MediaCodec output queues — Samsung SM-S918W per Crashlytics).
2. Open the app. Navigate: **video editor → video metadata (preview / cover) → pooled video feed**.
3. Repeat the breadcrumb 10–20× per session.
4. Background the app while a video is playing on one of the editor / metadata screens.
5. Force-finish the activity from recents, or close the app.
6. Repeat across several launches.

Pre-fix: Crashlytics records the `FlutterJNI is not attached to native` exception under issue `d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a`. Volume is low (1.0.13: 1 user / 1 fatal in May 15 sample) because the race window is small, but it is **fatal** when it fires.

Post-fix: the editor / metadata / clip-preview screens render via the legacy `SurfaceTextureEntry` backend, which has no `ImageReader` and therefore cannot fire the offending callback after engine teardown.

## Out of Scope

- **`media_kit_video` Android backend hardening.** If the pooled-video-feed fallback (only reached when `InfiniteVideoFeed.isSupported` is `false`, which is not Android in production) has a parallel race family, it needs its own PR scoped to the third-party media_kit. Tracked separately when needed.
- **iOS sibling #4400** (FVP / FVPFrameUpdater / ProVideoEditorPlugin / VideoTextureOutput post-teardown callbacks).
- **Reflection-based `MediaCodec.flush()` synchronous fence.** PR #3762 rejected as overkill; not needed once this change takes the volume to zero.
- **Manually editing each of the 5 vulnerable callsites.** Default-flip is strictly cleaner — it covers future code too.

## Verification

Local:

- [x] `dart format` on changed Dart file — no churn
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` from `mobile/` — no issues
- [x] `flutter analyze` from `mobile/packages/divine_video_player` — no issues
- [x] `flutter test` from `mobile/packages/divine_video_player` — **154/154 pass**
- [x] `flutter test` from `mobile/packages/infinite_video_feed` — **150/150 pass**
- [x] Comprehensive callsite audit (`grep -rEn "useTexture\s*:\s*true"` across `mobile/`) — confirmed 5 vulnerable callsites all inherit the new default; only `infinite_video_feed` explicitly sets `useLegacySurface: true`; no callsite explicitly sets it to `false`.

Manual (requires real Android device — not run from this PR; recommended before / immediately after merge):

- [ ] Repeat the reproduction breadcrumb above 20× per build on a real Android device. Expected: no crash, no black-frame regression on the 5 affected screens.
- [ ] Post-release: watch Crashlytics issue `d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a` for ≥1 release. Expected: events drop to zero.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Risk Register

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vivo/Android 16 compositor event on the 5 affected screens causes black surface (no surface-recreate callback) | Low — those flows are short-lived and not permission-dialog-heavy | Recoverable (user navigates back/forward) | Strictly better than a fatal crash; if a Crashlytics black-frame signal emerges on those screens, the callsite can explicitly pass `useLegacySurface: false` with a documented justification |
| Hidden external consumer relying on the old default | None — workspace package, no external consumers | — | — |
| Native default drift (Kotlin still `false`) | None — Dart always passes the value | — | Documented in the KDoc rewrite |
| Existing tests pin the old default | None — confirmed via audit; tests don't assert default value | — | All 154 + 150 tests green |

title: perf(inbox): remove _overlayLatestMessages once write-path fix has aged in
body:
## Summary

PR #4296 fixed the N+1 read-path debt in \`DmRepository\` by:

1. Replacing the per-conversation \`getMessagesForConversation(limit: 1)\` fan-out with a single batched \`getLatestMessagesForConversations\` query (Option A).
2. Fixing the write-path drift in \`upsertConversation\` so out-of-order gift-wrap arrivals no longer overwrite a newer denormalized preview (Option B).

The \`_overlayLatestMessages\` method and its \`asyncMap\` calls on \`watchAcceptedConversations\` / \`watchPotentialRequests\` were kept as a transitional safety net for existing installations that may have stale \`conversations\` rows written by app versions prior to the write-path fix.

## What remains

Once the write-path fix has been live long enough that no device in the wild can still have stale preview rows from older code, the following can be deleted entirely:

- \`DmRepository._overlayLatestMessages\`
- The \`.asyncMap(_overlayLatestMessages)\` call in \`watchAcceptedConversations\`
- The \`.asyncMap(_overlayLatestMessages)\` call in \`watchPotentialRequests\`
- \`DirectMessagesDao.getLatestMessagesForConversations\` (only called from the overlay)
- The corresponding tests for the overlay behaviour in \`dm_repository_test.dart\`

At that point the conversation-watch queries become the sole source of truth for inbox previews, and the inbox read path requires zero extra queries per emit.

## Acceptance criteria

- \`watchAcceptedConversations\` and \`watchPotentialRequests\` emit directly from the \`conversations\` watch query with no \`asyncMap\` overlay.
- The write-path fix has been validated as sufficient: inbox previews are correct without the overlay.
- All existing inbox tests still pass.

title: fix(crashlytics): stop Android FlutterJNI detach renderer crash after video surfaces
body:
## Crashlytics evidence

Crashlytics issue: `d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a`

Console: https://console.firebase.google.com/project/openvine-co/crashlytics/app/android:co.openvine.app/issues/d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a?&time=1776614940000:1777219740000

Window queried with Firebase MCP: `2026-04-19T16:09:00Z` to `2026-04-26T16:09:00Z`

Impact in that window:

- Events: 31
- Impacted users: 15
- Sessions: 31
- First seen: `1.0.4`
- Last seen: `1.0.8`
- Signal: regressed; Crashlytics says it was closed on `2026-03-08` and regressed on `2026-03-19` in `1.0.7 (497)`.

Sample event:

- Event: `projects/972941478875/apps/1:972941478875:android:c716006682f92d9444b5fe/events/69EE0CF801F5000127E39EE7C625DF0C_2211500816387455056`
- Event time: `2026-04-26T13:12:38Z`
- App version: `1.0.8 (2513)`
- Device: Moto G Power 2025, Android `16`
- Process state: foreground
- Breadcrumb path: video-editor -> video-metadata -> pooled-video-feed repeated

Exception:

```text
java.lang.RuntimeException: Cannot execute operation because FlutterJNI is not attached to native.
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterJNI.ensureAttachedToNative (FlutterJNI.java:515)
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterJNI.scheduleFrame (FlutterJNI.java:1013)
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer.scheduleEngineFrame (FlutterRenderer.java:1324)
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer$ImageReaderSurfaceProducer.onImage (FlutterRenderer.java:633)
at FlutterRenderer$ImageReaderSurfaceProducer$PerImageReader.lambda$new$0 (FlutterRenderer.java:517)
at android.media.ImageReader$1.run (ImageReader.java:951)
```

## Start here

This is not the already-filed back navigation issue by itself. Existing issue #2796/PR #2795 guarded app MethodChannel back navigation after engine detach. This crash is in Flutter renderer / `ImageReaderSurfaceProducer`, probably tied to Android platform views or texture-backed video surfaces still producing frames after engine detach/surface disposal.

Likely code areas:

- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/android/src/main/kotlin/com/divinevideo/divine_video_player/DivineVideoPlayerInstance.kt`
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/android/src/main/kotlin/com/divinevideo/divine_video_player/DivineVideoPlayerViewFactory.kt`
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/lib/src/divine_video_player_widget.dart`
- `mobile/packages/pooled_video_player` lifecycle if pooled feed uses platform/texture rendering on Android.
- `mobile/android/app/src/main/kotlin/co/openvine/app/MainActivity.kt` only if engine/activity lifecycle ordering is involved.

Relevant local context:

- `DivineVideoPlayerInstance.dispose()` removes callbacks/listeners and releases `textureEntry`.
- Android platform views use `PlatformViewLink` / `AndroidViewSurface` in `divine_video_player_widget.dart`.
- `DivineVideoPlayerPlugin` pauses players on lifecycle pause/resume but only disposes all on engine detach.

## Investigation requirements

Follow root-cause first. Do not assume the previous FlutterJNI back-button fix covers this.

- Reproduce or instrument Android lifecycle while video editor/metadata and pooled feed surfaces are active.
- Trace whether `ImageReaderSurfaceProducer` corresponds to `Texture` usage, Android hybrid composition, or Flutter engine internals triggered by our video widgets.
- Verify disposal order: Flutter widget removed -> platform view disposed -> ExoPlayer surface cleared -> texture released -> engine detached.
- Confirm whether any `Surface`, `SurfaceTextureEntry`, `PlayerView`, or ExoPlayer instance can emit frame callbacks after the Flutter engine is detached.
- Compare event variants in Crashlytics if needed; there are multiple variants under this same issue.

## Suggested fix direction

Possible areas to validate:

- Ensure every Android video surface clears the player and releases the surface before engine/activity detach.
- Add lifecycle-aware stop/dispose guards for video players on `onDetachedFromActivity`, not only `onDetachedFromEngine`.
- Avoid retaining `PlayerView` / `Surface` references beyond view disposal.
- If using texture output, explicitly detach the video surface and stop rendering before `textureEntry.release()`.

## Verification

- Add Android unit tests where practical around plugin/view dispose ordering.
- Run `mobile/packages/divine_video_player` tests and relevant Android tests.
- Manually test rapid navigation: video editor -> metadata -> pooled feed -> background/foreground -> close app.
- After release, confirm Crashlytics issue `d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a` stops receiving events.
